short: Fundamental misunderstanding of oneself and reality — the root of bondage.
beginner: Avidya is not lack of information but a basic mistake about who we are and what the world is — like taking the temporary for permanent, or the body for the self. Many traditions say it is the root of suffering.
what: Avidya is named as the first cause of bondage across many Indian systems. Yoga defines it as taking the impermanent, impure, painful and not-self as permanent, pure, pleasant and self, and lists it as the root of all afflictions. In Advaita it is the beginningless ignorance that superimposes the not-self on the Self. In Buddhism it heads the twelve links of dependent origination. The Gita speaks of knowledge covered by ignorance and dispelled by knowledge like the sun.
scholar: Advaita's theory of adhyasa (superimposition), set out in Shankara's introduction to his Brahma Sutra commentary, is the classic analysis. Post-Shankara debates concern avidya's locus and object. Buddhist avijja is non-knowledge of the four noble truths. Yoga Sutra 2.5 gives the fourfold definition noted above.

perspectives.view: Ignorance is the superimposition of body, mind and world on the Self; only knowledge, not action, can remove it.
Avidya is the first and root affliction (klesha), mistaking the impermanent and not-self for the permanent and self.
Ignorance of the nature of suffering and its cause is the first link in the chain that keeps rebirth going.
Bondage is due to beginningless karma, which contracts the soul's knowledge; removal is by God's grace through devotion rather than by knowledge alone.

follow.note: A short Upanishad that pairs and contrasts knowledge and ignorance.
Knowledge is covered by ignorance, and beings are deluded.
Knowledge dispels ignorance and reveals the supreme, like the sun.
Avidya as the root of all afflictions.
Ignorance as superimposition of the not-self on the Self.
Ignorance as the first link in the Buddhist chain.
